items.title: Digital Asset AFSL No-Action Deadline – 30 Sep 2026
items.desc: ASIC extended its no-action position for digital asset businesses to 30 September 2026. Firms must lodge an AFSL application, obtain a variation, or enter an authorised representative arrangement by this date or risk breaching financial services laws.

items.title: Employee Entitlement Schemes – AFSL Required from 1 Sep 2026
items.desc: Operators of employee entitlement schemes must hold an AFS licence from 1 September 2026. ASIC ended 25 years of regulatory relief in this area — unlicensed operators face enforcement action.

items.title: FS70 / FS71 – Disclosing Entities Due 30 Sep 2026
items.desc: AFS licensees that are disclosing entities must lodge FS70/71 (profit & loss, balance sheet, auditor's report) by 30 September 2026. All other entities have until 31 October 2026.

items.title: Annual Financial Report (Ch 2M) – Due 30 Sep 2026
items.desc: Annual financial report, directors' report and auditor's report must be lodged with ASIC by 30 September 2026 (Chapter 2M, Corporations Act). Non-disclosing entities have until 31 October.

items.title: Derivative Client Money Report – Due 31 Oct 2026
items.desc: AFSL holders with derivative retail client money must lodge the annual client money data report with ASIC by 31 October 2026.

items.title: Digital Assets Framework – AFSL Applications Open Apr 2027
items.desc: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 passed. DAP and TCP operators can lodge AFSL applications from April 2027 with full compliance required by October 2027. ASIC released an 18-month roadmap.

items.title: Annual Compliance Report – New FY Deadline from 2027
items.desc: AUSTRAC has moved annual compliance reports to a financial year basis. No report is required for Jan–Jun 2026. The first report under the new cycle is due 30 September 2027 for FY2026–27.

items.title: Tranche 2 Entities – Compliance Obligations Now in Effect
items.desc: Lawyers, accountants, real estate professionals and jewellers newly regulated from 1 July 2026. Must have an AML/CTF program, compliance officer, and staff training in place. AUSTRAC enforcement begins.

items.title: New TTR and SMR Reporting Forms – Live from 1 Jul 2026
items.desc: Updated threshold transaction report and suspicious matter report forms now available. Existing entities may continue using old forms until 30 March 2029 — transition at your own pace.

items.title: AUSTRAC Independent Review Obligations – 12-Month Window
items.desc: Entities with higher ML/TF risk must complete an independent review of their AML/CTF program within 12 months of the 31 March 2026 reform commencement. Review scope and timing should be confirmed now.

items.title: AUSTRAC Guidance on 2026 AML/CTF Reforms Released
items.desc: AUSTRAC and Minter Ellison have published practical guidance clarifying obligations under the reformed AML/CTF Act. Review updated guidance on customer due diligence, program structure, and record-keeping.

items.title: AER 2026–27 Compliance & Enforcement Priorities Released
items.desc: AER published its 2026–27 priorities: vulnerable consumer outcomes, smart meter rollout protection, power system security, competition and network safety, and Part 10 National Gas Rules reporting compliance.

items.title: Retailer Authorisation Consultation – Closes 21 Sep 2026
items.desc: AER published Yurringa Energy's application for electricity retailer authorisation. Public consultation closes Monday 21 September 2026. Existing retailers should monitor new entrant activity.

items.title: Minimum Disconnection Amount Raised – Effective 1 Jul 2026
items.desc: AER increased the minimum amount owed before a retailer may disconnect a customer under NECF from $300 to $500, effective 1 July 2026. Review disconnection procedures and system thresholds.

items.title: AER 2025–26 Compliance & Enforcement Annual Report Released
items.desc: AER released its annual report covering 2025–26 enforcement activities. Review findings relevant to portfolio companies with energy retail authorisations or network connections.

items.title: Rate of Return Instrument Review – Final Decision Dec 2026
items.desc: AER's 2026 RORI review is ongoing. Final decision expected December 2026, setting allowed returns on capital for regulated electricity and gas networks for the next regulatory cycle.
